recentItems.title: Birth of Sumatran tiger cubs at Greek zoo offers hope for endangered species
recentItems.description:
(8 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Spata, Greece - 8 September 2026
1. Various of Sumatran tiger mother and her three two-month-old cubs
2. Sign identifying Sumatran tiger
3. Sign announcing cubs' birth dated 3 July 2026
4. Various of tiger cub being carried by zookeepers
5. Tiger cub being brought into clinic for medical examination
6. Various of cub under examination, veterinarian Arsenoi Psaroudaki
7. Cub receiving vaccination 
8. Close-up of tiger cub
9. SOUNDBITE (English) Dr. Arsenoi Psaroudaki, zoo and wildlife veterinarian:
"When the cubs were first born, we don't come into contact with them because obviously these first weeks are very important for them to bond with their mother.  But we did give them visual health checks, and we did go in and have a look and make sure that everything is going well. But this is the first time we actually handled them in the clinic and they had a proper sort of physical exam."
10. Various of cub in examination room, receiving microchip
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Dr. Arsenoi Psaroudaki, zoo and wildlife veterinarian:
“The tigers don’t like to be handled. They’re very wild. They only come into direct contact with their mother, which means that we try and do everything as quick as possible to keep it as stress-free as possible for them." 
12. Various of tiger cub being weighed
13. Various of tiger cub being taken out of clinic
14. Various of tiger cub growling, paws
15. Various of cub being carried in golf cart
16. Signboard of zoo reading (Greek) "Attica Zoological Park"
17. Closeup of zoo map, including location of Sumatran Tiger 
18. Tiger and cubs
19. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Theodoros Babilis, head keeper of cats and monkeys at Attica Zoological Park:
“The Sumatran tiger is one of the most threatened tiger species in the world, and among felines in general. We're talking about 400 to 500 animals recorded in the wild, so we're dealing with a critically endangered population."
20. Tiger cub
21. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Theodoros Babilis, head keeper of cats and monkeys at Attica Zoological Park:
"At zoos we are effectively maintaining a safety population of the animals so that in the future, there can be potential reintroductions of this species into the wild.”
22. Tiger walking 
STORYLINE:
The world’s most endangered tigers have started a family in Greece — offering hope for a predator that is rapidly vanishing from the wild.

Three 2-month-old Sumatran tiger cubs received identification microchips and their first vaccinations Tuesday at a zoo near Athens, as part of a global effort to build a backup population.

The Sumatran tiger — classified as critically endangered by the United Nations and conservation groups — is found only on the Indonesian island of Sumatra, which is slightly larger than Sweden. 

As few as 400 are believed to remain in the wild, mainly because of aggressive forest clearing.

“The Sumatran tiger is one of the most threatened tiger species in the world, and among felines in general,” said Theodoros Babilis, head keeper of cats and monkeys at Attica Zoological Park.

Zoos in Europe and elsewhere are maintaining a safety population, he said, “so that in the future there can be potential reintroductions of this species into the wild.”

The Sumatran tiger is the smallest tiger species in the world, but males can still grow up to 2.55 meters (8.4 feet) long and weigh as much as 140 kilograms (309 pounds).

Skilled swimmers and climbers, they use their dark stripes — unique to each animal, like a fingerprint — to hide in the dense forest as they hunt deer, wild pigs and smaller mammals.

recentItems.title: Casey Affleck arrives to promote 'Company,' showing in Venice Film Festival competition
recentItems.description:
(8 Sep 2026) 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Venice, Italy - 8 September 2026
1. Medium shot (left-right) Emily Alyn Lind, Adelaide Clemens, and Scoot McNairy
2. Zoom in Emily Alyn Lind
3. Medium shot Adelaide Clemens, pull out to medium shot Clemens and McNairy
4.  Tracking shot Clemens and McNairy leaving jetty
5. Various shots Casey Affleck posing for photographs, then leaving jetty
6. Close-up Affleck signing autographs
7. Tracking shot Caylee Cowan arriving and signing autographs


STORYLINE:
Actor/director Casey Affleck has arrived in Venice to promote his gothic horror, "Company."

The movie, which is showing in competition at the film festival, stars Nick Nolte, Emily Alyn Lind and Ben Mendelsohn. 

Lind plays Evelyn - a mysterious woman who arrives uninvited at a holiday gathering and tells the story of Tom, an ageing hermit (Nolte) who rescues a stranded actress during a Colorado blizzard in 1953.

The film, which is co-written and co-produced by Affleck, also stars Scoot McNairy, Adelaide Clemens and Affleck's partner, Caylee Cowan.

It is one of 21 films competing for the festival's top prize, the Golden Lion.

recentItems.description:

STORYLINE:

1. SOT Ronan Keating, including soundbites: 
"It was fantastic, it's always difficult being the first act on a show like this today, early in the day, three o'clock, but they were up for it, they loved it, they were on their feet halfway through the set having a good time, they loved it."
"Fantastic, brilliant, loving every minute of it, we go to Australia next week, take it to Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and the Middle East, it's a World tour (next single?) end of August, 'Love it When We Do'"

recentItems.title: Samsung debuts new mid-range phone with AI functions IFA tech show
recentItems.description:
(8 Sep 2026) 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Berlin, Germany - 2 September 2026

1. Various of Samsung Galaxy S26 FE smartphone on display at Samsung Connect event
2. Various of Samsung worker demonstrating new Galaxy S26 FE smartphone’s AI functionalities
3. New Samsung Galaxy S26 FE smartphone on display
4. Setup shot of Benjamin Braun, chief marketing officer, Samsung Europe, demonstrating photo feature
UPSOUND (English): "So, I'm filming Simon, I don't have a tripod, and say I'm running after him on a sports field and it becomes really wobbly. You see how wobbly it is here? I can even turn it around, do a full 360 turn of the phone, still filming Simon. And then the AI will make this all stable."

5. SOUNDBITE (English) Benjamin Braun, chief marketing officer, Samsung Europe:
"We have just released the Samsung S26FE. It is lower cost. It's more affordable, so more people can buy it, but we haven't skimped on the AI, it is ram-packed with really helpful AI. I'll give you a couple of examples, if we're doing this interview instead of typing it up, it simply listens to us, it writes it all up, It can even summarize it and translate it into in my case Swedish or French or Spanish or since we're in Berlin into German, you become a global traveler with a translator in your pocket."

6. Various of Samsung worker demonstrating new Galaxy S26 FE smartphone’s AI functionalities
7. SOUNDBITE (English) Benjamin Braun, chief marketing officer, Samsung Europe:
"AI is actually a matter of democracy. We want at Samsung as many people as possible to have access to AI, and therefore we're opening it up to as many products as possible. Not only that, we're even pushing out AI to products that you already bought from Samsung that might be one or two years old. We're updating them over the air so you get free AI."

8. Pan of Samsung Connect event
9. Mid of sign, reading (English): “Samsung Connect. Home Appliance. AI Home”
10. Various of new Samsung Bespoke AI Washer 
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Benjamin Braun, chief marketing officer, Samsung Europe:
"Things that are repetitive and mundane can really become a little bit easier with AI. The Samsung washing machine has AI so when I take the school uniforms for my three kids and chuck them in there, it knows how dirty they are and therefore only uses the amount of water, energy, time and detergent that's actually needed. Also when it's done, it sends me a notification to my watch or to my phone so I can go and hang up the school uniforms so they're ready for the next day."

12. Pan of Samsung Connect event
13. Pan of Samsung Z Fold8 smartphone 
14. Various of Braun demonstrating Samsung foldable handset
15. SOUNDBITE (English) Benjamin Braun, chief marketing officer, Samsung Europe:
"People want bigger and bigger mobile phones, but our pockets are not becoming any bigger. So what do we do? We fold the display. This is my Swedish passport, and behind it is the latest Samsung Fold8 phone. It's beautiful, and it unfolds like that. Look at that screen. It's super, but it's also a screen up front. And what I really like with this is you can watch 25 hours of video, so we can fly from Berlin, where we are today, back to London. Back to Sweden, to Korea, jump in an Uber, and go to a restaurant and still have battery left over to finish whatever you're watching on Netflix. And also, it's really great for multitasking. This is a super device, and what we're seeing, people are loving it. We're outselling last year's version with 15%."

16. Various of Samsung Z Flip8 foldable handsets on display
17. Samsung Connect logo on screen

STORYLINE:

recentItems.title: LG shows vision of ‘zero labor’ AI home at IFA in Berlin
recentItems.description:
(8 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS

Berlin, Germany - 3 September 2026

1. Various of LG presentation at IFA consumer electronics show, LG’s CLOiD home robot conducting an orchestra of home appliances
2. IFA attendee filming presentation 
3. LG’s CLOiD home robot
4. Various of home appliances
5. LG’s CLOiD home robot
6. Pan of LG’s AI Home area
7. Mid of sign, reading (English): “LG AI Home”
8. Attendee walking through AI Home
9. LG logo
10. SOUNDBITE (English) Grace Park, senior manager, LG Electronics:
"We're trying to show the visitors the vision of AI Home, which is we have a lot of products with AI features and that combined together, we can make a complete orchestrated home with AI features and also the agents that we are using, ThinQ ON and ThinQ Claw. So, what we're trying tell the customers in Europe is that with all the AI feature products, we can put it all together at home and have your life made better and easier, so you don't have to do that much of house chores or anything."

11. Various of bed and app demonstration
12. Various of AI washing machine
13. Various of demonstration of oven, recognising different dishes and recommending cooking time
14. Camera view inside oven
15. Exhibitor operating oven
16. Smart stove
17. SOUNDBITE (English) Grace Park, senior manager, LG Electronics:
"Let's say if you're watching TV, and your laundry is done, you can have all the notice in the TV and also you can, with ThinQ Claw, with your text messaging, you can also say: can you run a pre-wash in my washing machine and then you can text it and also you can say it by voice control. And you can also control your oven with the Claw or ThinQ ON the agent. So, you can pre-heat your oven by just telling ThinQ ON with voice control and order the oven to pre-heat."

18. Various of demonstration of fridge 
19. Fan
20. SOUNDBITE (English) Grace Park, senior manager, LG Electronics:
"Right now, in Seoul, we are doing these kind of features. It's already launched. I think it's not really futuristic, but in the future, what our vision is, that our home is a zero-labor home, where we don't have to think about anything, but they will do whatever. You know, you just stay. I know we're going be all bored to death, but you know. We envision that our AI home, it will do whatever it takes, we don't have to work hard as much as we do right now."

21. Pan of LG’s AI Home area
22. Various of shower
23. Pull focus of LG logo
STORYLINE:
LEADIN:

At Berlin’s IFA consumer electronics show, South Korean electronics giant LG is demonstrating its “zero labor" home vision.

It comes with an expanded AI ecosystem of connected devices and appliances.

STORYLINE:

It’s an orchestra of home appliances, with artificial intelligence as the conductor.

South Korea’s LG says AI homes are no longer science fiction, but an increasing reality, thanks to its collection of connected home appliances.

The company has this AI home demonstration at the IFA tech show in Berlin.

"We're trying to show the visitors the vision of AI Home, which is we have a lot of products with AI features and that combined together, we can make a complete orchestrated home with AI features,” explains LG senior manager Grace Park.

“With all the AI feature products, we can put it all together at home and have your life made better and easier, so you don't have to do that much of house chores or anything."

LG says its next-generation AI home hub - LG ThinQ ON - connects appliances, spaces and services into one single, cohesive system.















AP video by James Brooks

"We are aiming to bring every robot to your families, as your personal robot, this is our aim. And the very first theory is that we are not bringing some cold machine into your family, but friendly and soft family members to your families."

"We are designing into the indoor family scenarios. For example, we have to play games with our kids, accompany with elderly, and take photos of our whole family.
